cards.hypothesis: Subjects with blunted cortisol reactivity exhibit systematically lower EDA amplitude during stress, causing their nonconformity scores to fall outside the calibration distribution used by Mondrian categories.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Blunted HPA-axis reactivity reduces sympathetic arousal magnitude, producing EDA responses that are statistically indistinguishable from baseline in the feature space, leading Mondrian taxonomy to assign them to incorrect strata.
cards.causal_path: Low cortisol reactivity -> reduced EDA phasic amplitude -> feature vector proximity to baseline cluster -> Mondrian category misassignment -> calibration quantile mismatch -> undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage stems from random calibration set variability rather than systematic physiological differences.
cards.rival_prediction: Undercoverage subjects will not show consistently blunted cortisol or EDA responses across repeated stress exposures.
cards.distinguishing_test: Measure cortisol and EDA reactivity in a second stress session; blunted responders should replicate undercoverage while random variability should not.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Literature reports ~30% of population shows blunted cortisol reactivity; effect on EDA amplitude is well-documented (r ~ 0.4-0.5).
minimum_data_needed: WESAD EDA and cortisol measures per subject
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects in lowest cortisol reactivity tertile will have coverage rates <80% at nominal 90% level.
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between cortisol reactivity tertile and per-subject coverage rate (Spearman rho > -0.2).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Spearman correlation between cortisol_reactivity_auc and per-subject coverage rate; logistic regression predicting undercoverage (binary) from cortisol tertile controlling for age/sex.
cards.falsification_test: Re-run Mondrian with cortisol-reactivity-stratified taxonomy; if undercoverage persists in blunted responders, mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Wrist-worn sensor contact quality varies systematically across subjects due to wrist circumference and skin properties, causing EDA signal attenuation that distorts feature extraction for specific individuals.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Poor sensor-skin contact increases impedance, attenuating high-frequency EDA components used in feature extraction, shifting feature vectors toward baseline and causing systematic miscalibration for affected subjects.
cards.causal_path: Large wrist circumference / dry skin -> increased electrode impedance -> EDA signal attenuation -> reduced feature discriminability -> Mondrian category misassignment -> undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is driven by physiological differences, not sensor artifacts.
cards.rival_prediction: Signal quality metrics (SNR, impedance) will not correlate with coverage rates after controlling for physiological reactivity.
cards.distinguishing_test: Correlate baseline impedance and SNR with per-subject coverage; sensor artifact hypothesis predicts strong negative correlation.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Impedance can vary 10x across subjects; EDA amplitude attenuation directly scales with impedance. Prior work shows >50% feature degradation at high impedance.
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with baseline impedance >75th percentile will have coverage rates at least 15 percentage points lower than those <25th percentile.
cards.failure_condition: No significant difference in coverage between high and low impedance groups (p > 0.05, two-sample t-test).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear regression: coverage_rate ~ baseline_impedance + wrist_circumference + skin_type; mediation analysis testing SNR as mediator.
cards.falsification_test: Re-process raw EDA with impedance-corrected feature extraction; if undercoverage disappears for high-impedance subjects, original mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Subjects exhibiting delayed stress recovery show non-stationary nonconformity scores within the calibration window, violating the exchangeability assumption for their Mondrian stratum.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Prolonged physiological arousal after stressor offset creates a temporal trend in nonconformity scores during calibration, causing the empirical quantile to underestimate true variability for subsequent test points.
cards.causal_path: Delayed recovery -> positive temporal trend in nonconformity scores during calibration -> empirical quantile too low -> test points exceed quantile -> undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage reflects inherent subject difficulty, not temporal non-stationarity.
cards.rival_prediction: Nonconformity scores will show no systematic temporal trend within calibration windows for undercovered subjects.
cards.distinguishing_test: Fit linear trend to nonconformity scores within each subject's calibration window; test if slope predicts coverage deficit.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Recovery time constants vary 2-3x across individuals; simulation studies show 10-20% coverage deficit from moderate trends (slope ~0.01 per trial).
minimum_data_needed: Per-trial nonconformity scores with temporal ordering
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with recovery time constant > median will show positive nonconformity score trends (slope > 0) and coverage deficits >10%.
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between recovery time constant and nonconformity score trend slope (p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Mixed-effects model: nonconformity_score ~ trial_index + (trial_index | subject); extract per-subject slopes; correlate with coverage deficit.
cards.falsification_test: Use online conformal prediction with adaptive windowing; if undercoverage persists for slow-recovery subjects, mechanism falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Self-reported stress labels (VAS) for certain subjects systematically diverge from physiological ground truth due to interoceptive awareness differences, creating label noise that corrupts Mondrian category calibration.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Low interoceptive accuracy causes subjects to under-report stress during high physiological arousal, assigning 'low stress' labels to high-arousal states; Mondrian taxonomy learns incorrect category-conditional distributions.
cards.causal_path: Low interoceptive_accuracy -> VAS_rating < physiological_arousal -> label_noise_in_calibration -> Mondrian_category_distribution_shift -> test_coverage_deficit
cards.rival_explanation: Physiological features are simply non-predictive for some subjects, not mislabeled.
cards.rival_prediction: Label discrepancy will not correlate with coverage; feature predictive power (AUC) will be low for undercovered subjects regardless of labels.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compute label discrepancy = |VAS - physiological_arousal|; test if it predicts coverage deficit better than feature AUC.
cards.effect_size_rationale: No prior work quantifies label noise impact on Mondrian coverage; would need pilot data estimating interoceptive accuracy distribution and label discrepancy magnitude in WESAD.
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects in lowest interoceptive accuracy quartile will have coverage rates <75% at nominal 90%.
cards.failure_condition: Interoceptive accuracy shows no association with coverage deficit (Spearman rho > -0.15).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Quantile regression: coverage_rate ~ interoceptive_accuracy + physiological_arousal_mean; test interaction with label_discrepancy.
cards.falsification_test: Re-train Mondrian using only physiological labels (unsupervised clustering); if undercoverage persists for low-interoception subjects, mechanism falsified.

cards.hypothesis: The Mondrian taxonomy (based on stress condition labels) fails to capture subject-specific physiological response phenotypes, causing heterogeneous subjects to share categories with incompatible nonconformity distributions.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Taxonomy categories (baseline/stress/amusement/meditation) pool physiologically distinct responders (e.g., 'high reactors' vs 'low reactors') into same stratum, violating category-conditional exchangeability.
cards.causal_path: Coarse taxonomy -> within-category physiological heterogeneity -> bimodal nonconformity distribution -> empirical quantile misses tail -> undercoverage for minority phenotype
cards.rival_explanation: Taxonomy is adequate; undercoverage stems from finite-sample variability in small categories.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deficits will be symmetric across phenotypes within categories and shrink with larger calibration sets.
cards.distinguishing_test: Cluster subjects by physiological response pattern; test if coverage varies significantly across clusters within same taxonomy category.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Phenotype misalignment can cause >30% coverage gaps; Mondrian theory guarantees coverage only under category-conditional exchangeability.
cards.testable_prediction: At least one taxonomy category will contain >2 physiological clusters with coverage difference >20 percentage points.
cards.failure_condition: All physiological clusters within each taxonomy category have coverage within 5% of nominal level.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Gaussian mixture modeling on stress-response features; ANOVA of coverage_rate ~ cluster * taxonomy_category; post-hoc Tukey HSD.
cards.falsification_test: Refine taxonomy using physiological clusters as categories; if undercoverage eliminated, original taxonomy was cause; if persists, mechanism falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Calibration sets for certain subjects are contaminated by anticipatory arousal during baseline periods, shifting the nonconformity distribution and causing undercoverage during actual stress.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Subjects with high trait anxiety show elevated physiology during 'baseline' due to anticipation, making baseline nonconformity scores resemble stress; Mondrian learns inflated baseline quantile, causing stress trials to exceed it.
cards.causal_path: High_trait_anxiety -> anticipatory_arousal_during_baseline -> elevated_baseline_nonconformity -> inflated_baseline_quantile -> stress_trials_exceed_quantile -> undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage reflects true stress response variability, not baseline contamination.
cards.rival_prediction: Baseline nonconformity scores will not correlate with trait anxiety or predict stress coverage deficit.
cards.distinguishing_test: Correlate baseline nonconformity mean with trait anxiety and with stress coverage deficit; mediation analysis.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Trait anxiety explains ~15% variance in anticipatory arousal; simulation suggests 10-15% coverage deficit from 0.5 SD baseline shift.
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with STAI-T > 75th percentile will have baseline nonconformity scores >0.5 SD above mean and stress coverage <80%.
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between trait anxiety and baseline nonconformity (p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear regression: baseline_nonconformity_mean ~ trait_anxiety; logistic regression: undercoverage ~ baseline_nonconformity_mean + trait_anxiety.
cards.falsification_test: Exclude first baseline period from calibration; if undercoverage disappears for high-anxiety subjects, mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Strong temporal autocorrelation in physiological residuals violates the exchangeability assumption for subjects with high autonomic stability, causing Mondrian's i.i.d.-based quantiles to be anticonservative.
cards.proposed_mechanism: High autonomic stability produces highly predictable physiological trajectories (low innovation variance), creating long-range dependence in nonconformity scores that makes empirical quantiles underestimate future variability.
cards.causal_path: High_autonomic_stability -> low_residual_innovation_variance -> high_nonconformity_autocorrelation -> effective_sample_size_reduction -> quantile_underestimation -> undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to distributional shift, not autocorrelation.
cards.rival_prediction: Block bootstrap coverage estimates will match nominal levels if distributional shift is absent.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare standard conformal coverage vs. block bootstrap coverage estimates per subject; autocorrelation hypothesis predicts block bootstrap reveals true undercoverage.
cards.effect_size_rationale: AR(1) coefficients >0.7 reduce effective sample size by ~50%; coverage deficit scales with sqrt(n_eff/n) ~ 10-15% for n=100.
minimum_data_needed: Per-trial nonconformity scores in temporal order
Per-subject autonomic stability metric (HRV RMSSD consistency)
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with AR(1) coefficient >0.7 will have actual coverage <85% at nominal 90% while block bootstrap estimates match nominal.
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between AR(1) coefficient and coverage deficit (Spearman rho < 0.2).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Fit AR(1) to nonconformity scores per subject; compute effective n; regression: coverage_deficit ~ 1/sqrt(effective_n) + autonomic_stability.
cards.falsification_test: Apply conformal prediction with block-calibration (using blocks matching autocorrelation length); if undercoverage eliminated, mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Subjects with high movement artifact burden during stress have corrupted EDA/ACC features that systematically bias nonconformity scores downward, creating false confidence in predictions.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Movement artifacts introduce structured noise that the base classifier misinterprets as signal patterns, producing spuriously low nonconformity scores for contaminated stress trials that fall within calibration quantiles despite being unreliable.
cards.rival_explanation: Movement artifacts increase nonconformity scores (making coverage conservative), not decrease them.
cards.rival_prediction: Artifact-contaminated trials will have higher nonconformity scores than clean trials.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare nonconformity score distributions for artifact-flagged vs clean stress trials; test direction of shift.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Artifact contamination affects ~20-40% of stress trials in wrist-worn data; feature corruption can reduce nonconformity by 0.5-1 SD in classifier output space.
cards.testable_prediction: Artifact-contaminated stress trials will show nonconformity scores 0.3+ SD lower than clean trials and coverage >95% (false coverage).
cards.failure_condition: Artifact-contaminated trials have equal or higher nonconformity scores than clean trials (p > 0.05, one-sided).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Two-sample t-test: nonconformity_clean vs nonconformity_artifact; logistic regression: artifact_flag ~ nonconformity_score; coverage comparison by artifact status.
cards.falsification_test: Re-run Mondrian after removing artifact-contaminated trials from calibration; if undercoverage pattern reverses, mechanism confirmed; if unchanged, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Individual baseline drift in skin conductance level (SCL) across the experimental session causes feature distribution shift that disproportionately affects subjects with high tonic EDA variability.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Progressive SCL drift (due to hydration, temperature, or habituation) shifts the feature distribution for late-session trials relative to early-session calibration data, causing miscalibration for subjects with steep drift slopes.
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is uniform across trial order, not concentrated in late trials.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage will not differ between early and late stress trials for any subject group.
cards.distinguishing_test: Split stress trials into early/late halves; test interaction between drift slope and trial half on coverage.
cards.effect_size_rationale: SCL drift typically 0.01-0.05 µS/min; feature shift accumulates to ~0.5 SD over 30min; expected coverage deficit 5-10% for high-drift subjects.
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects in top SCL drift quartile will show >10% coverage difference between early and late stress trials.
cards.failure_condition: No interaction between drift slope and trial half on coverage (p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Mixed logistic regression: coverage ~ trial_half * drift_slope + (1|subject); test interaction term.
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate Mondrian using sliding window (last 20 trials); if undercoverage eliminated for high-drift subjects, mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Rare subject-condition combinations (e.g., specific subject x meditation condition) have insufficient calibration samples, causing high variance in empirical quantiles and sporadic undercoverage.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Mondrian categories with few calibration points per subject produce noisy quantile estimates; by chance, some subject-category pairs get underestimated quantiles, leading to undercoverage that appears subject-specific but is actually a small-sample artifact.
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage reflects true physiological differences, not sampling variability.
cards.rival_prediction: Undercoverage will persist with increased calibration data; it will not correlate with calibration count.
cards.distinguishing_test: Simulate coverage as function of calibration n via subsampling; test if observed undercoverage matches small-sample variance prediction.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Depends on actual calibration counts per subject-category in WESAD; need to compute empirical distribution of n_per_cell to estimate quantile SE.
minimum_data_needed: Calibration set sizes per subject per Mondrian category
cards.testable_prediction: Subject-category cells with calibration n < 15 will show coverage variance >2x that of cells with n > 30.
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between calibration count and coverage variance across subject-category cells (p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Levene's test for equality of coverage variance across calibration count bins; beta-binomial model for coverage ~ calibration_n.
cards.falsification_test: Pool calibration data across similar subjects (hierarchical Mondrian); if undercoverage disappears for low-n cells, mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified.
